root.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Classical Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 e6 5. Bxc4 c5

overview: Black hits the d4 pawn at once. The main line is 6.O-O a6 7.a4 Nc6 8.Qe2 cxd4 9.Rd1 Be7 10.exd4 O-O, leaving White with an isolated queen's pawn and active pieces and Black with a solid position and a target on d4. Other lines go 6.Nc3 or 7.Qe2 with ...b5 queenside play.

white_ideas.idea: Active pieces against an isolated queen's pawn, with Qe2, Rd1 and e4-e5 kingside ideas.
Pressure on the d-file and Black's king.

black_ideas.idea: Trade pieces and attack the d4 isolated pawn with ...Nb4, ...Nd5 and ...Bd7.

typical_structures.structure: Isolated queen's pawn on d4 for White against a Black pawn majority on the queenside.

character.notes: Fairly solid for Black, with a sound pawn structure and clear plans; not forcing.

structure.notes: Open lines for pieces and an IQP structure after cxd4.

level.notes: IQP play is a classic plan; theory moderate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 6.Nc3
sublines_that_differ.how: A sharper line with more transposition options.

character.reason: Neither especially forcing nor especially hard to crack.

gambit.reason: White regains the pawn by force.

structure.reason: QGA-style open lines, with d4 captured and IQP pieces active.

plans.reason: The IQP is the central structure.
